# Explain a system through requests, decisions and evidence

[← All question groups](../index.md) · `communication-system-explanation` · **Engineering Process & Communication** · Catalog level: senior

<p>Questions come from the preserved source notes. Reframing, assessment intent, senior signals and rubrics are editorial interpretations, not verified model answers or universal interviewer expectations. Follow-ups and the combined production exercise are agent additions. Reading this bank creates no learning record, score, completion or review schedule.</p>

## Start with one representative question

[S04-Q001](#S04-Q001)

<p>Draw a system you can explain and follow one request from the client to its final result. Where does responsibility pass between components?</p>

## One group objective and observable capabilities

<p>Give a direct architecture explanation whose choices can be defended in follow-up.</p>

<ul>
<li>Trace one browser request through UI, identity, gateway, backend, data and telemetry.</li>
<li>Explain one design choice and its rejected alternative using consequential constraints.</li>
<li>Adapt a trade-off explanation to the audience while preserving its technical limits.</li>
</ul>

**Prerequisites**

No catalog prerequisite. Establish the terms and scenario assumptions in the foundation questions before progressing; a published lesson is not evidence that you know them.

<p>Use a request to establish the system flow before explaining why its boundaries and technologies were chosen. Compare alternatives, translate the consequence for a non-specialist and use follow-ups to test each claim against failure and evidence.</p>

<a id="S06-SC001"></a>

### S06-SC001 · Mechanism

<p>Trace one request from a browser interaction through the backend and its dependencies to the HTTP response and resulting UI state.</p>

**Source:** [S06-SC001](../../sources/06-frontend-behavioral.md#cross-stack-request-flow)

<p>This editorial scenario ID identifies an existing unnumbered source scenario. Its steps and constraints are not separate source questions.</p>

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S06-SC001](../../sources/06-frontend-behavioral.md#cross-stack-request-flow)**

Open the source link for the complete original constraints. The scenario remains one source unit; its original Markdown is also preserved in the shared inventory.

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Connect all ten source stages: component/UI event; frontend service/client; authentication information; gateway/reverse proxy; ASP.NET Core middleware; routing and authorization; application/domain logic; EF Core/database or external dependency; telemetry; HTTP response and UI state update.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Explain a cross-stack request causally with clear responsibility and failure boundaries.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Use a generic Angular/ASP.NET Core example; mark optional components and telemetry observed across stages. State runtime versions and verify version-specific pipeline behavior in official documentation.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Preserves all ten stages while distinguishing the illustrative path from a universal physical order.</li>
<li>Connects a failure or latency symptom to observable evidence and the responsible boundary.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Lists layers without following data, authorization decisions or the UI outcome.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>Where would you look if the server completed the request but the screen stayed stale?</li>
<li>How would you identify which boundary consumed most of a slow request&#x27;s time?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S04-Q001"></a>

### S04-Q001 · Application

<p>Draw a system you can explain and follow one request from the client to its final result. Where does responsibility pass between components?</p>

**Source:** [S04-Q001](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#q001)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S04-Q001](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#q001)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Draw a system architecture and trace a request end-to-end.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Use the request to make the diagram meaningful: show the component that receives each step and the data it reads or changes.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Explain an end-to-end flow through clear ownership and state transitions.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Use a generic design or privacy-safe real example. State whether the final result is synchronous or arrives later.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Connect diagram arrows to specific request and data transitions.</li>
<li>Identify a failure boundary and the evidence needed to locate it.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Listing technologies without explaining how the request moves through them.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>If the response never arrives, which boundary would you investigate first?</li>
<li>How does the diagram change when a background worker produces the result?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S04-Q002"></a>

### S04-Q002 · Trade-offs

<p>For the system you drew, why did you choose these technologies and responsibility boundaries? What constraint would make you choose differently?</p>

**Source:** [S04-Q002](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#q002)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S04-Q002](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#q002)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Explain the technology choices and why the boundaries were selected.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Explain one consequential choice rather than defending every tool. A boundary separates who owns a rule, data or operational responsibility.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Defend an architectural choice using constraints and a credible alternative.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>State workload, team and deployment assumptions. Distinguish observed experience from a proposed design.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Connect the choice to a concrete requirement and an alternative rejected for a stated reason.</li>
<li>Name a cost and the evidence that would justify revisiting the boundary.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Presenting popularity or an architecture label as sufficient justification.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>Which change in requirements would invalidate this choice?</li>
<li>What would you measure before replacing the chosen technology?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S06-Q019"></a>

### S06-Q019 · Trade-offs

<p>Explain one design decision, the alternatives you considered, and why the constraints led you to choose that option.</p>

**Source:** [S06-Q019](../../sources/06-frontend-behavioral.md#q019)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S06-Q019](../../sources/06-frontend-behavioral.md#q019)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Explain a design decision and the alternatives you rejected.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Show the reasoning at the time of the decision, including a cost accepted by the chosen option. An alternative is a plausible competing approach, not a deliberately weak option.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Defend an engineering choice using constraints, alternatives and a decision boundary.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>State requirements and available evidence. Distinguish a genuine decision from a clearly labeled hypothetical design; omit confidential context and unsupported measurements.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Compares plausible alternatives against the same requirements.</li>
<li>States what evidence or changed constraint would justify revisiting the decision.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Claims the chosen pattern is universally best or dismisses alternatives without considering their fit.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>Which cost did you knowingly accept?</li>
<li>What changed condition would make an alternative preferable?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S06-Q024"></a>

### S06-Q024 · Trade-offs

<p>How would you explain a technical trade-off to a non-specialist so they can participate in the decision?</p>

**Source:** [S06-Q024](../../sources/06-frontend-behavioral.md#q024)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S06-Q024](../../sources/06-frontend-behavioral.md#q024)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Explain a technical trade-off clearly to a non-specialist.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Translate the engineering choice into its effect on the person&#x27;s goals while preserving the important mechanism and limits. A trade-off means accepting a cost to obtain a benefit under stated constraints.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Make an engineering choice understandable without removing the information needed to judge it.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>State the audience, decision and available evidence. Use a real privacy-safe example or label a hypothetical one; do not invent business impact.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Explains alternatives through consequences the audience can compare.</li>
<li>Checks understanding and states the uncertainty that could change the recommendation.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Replaces the explanation with jargon or an analogy that hides a decisive limitation.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>How would you check that the listener understood the cost being accepted?</li>
<li>Which technical detail must remain in the explanation to avoid a misleading decision?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S06-Q025"></a>

### S06-Q025 · Production decision

<p>When an interviewer challenges a technical claim you made, how would you answer using concrete constraints, failure modes and measurable evidence?</p>

**Source:** [S06-Q025](../../sources/06-frontend-behavioral.md#q025)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S06-Q025](../../sources/06-frontend-behavioral.md#q025)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Answer follow-up questions with concrete constraints, failure modes and measurable evidence.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Continue defending the current claim rather than changing topics. A failure mode is a specific way the mechanism can stop meeting its intended contract.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Keep a deeper technical explanation responsive, bounded and supported by evidence.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Use the actual claim and assumptions already established. Distinguish observed measurements from proposed tests; acknowledge uncertainty instead of manufacturing a result.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Answers the challenge directly and identifies the condition under which the claim holds.</li>
<li>Offers evidence that distinguishes outcomes and revises the claim if a counterexample applies.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Uses a polished bridge to evade the challenge or cites a measurement never performed.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What counterexample would invalidate your claim?</li>
<li>Which observation would distinguish your explanation from an alternative one?</li>
</ul>

</details>

## Combined production exercise — agent-added

<p>A non-specialist stakeholder asks why an Angular screen waits after submitting work to an ASP.NET Core API. Explain the request path and one design decision in plain language, then answer an engineer&#x27;s question about a delayed database call. Show what telemetry you would use and distinguish a proposed diagnosis from an observed result.</p>

## Short rubric — use only with an actual attempt

**Basic answer**

<p>Explains the components and one choice in an understandable sequence.</p>

**Senior answer**

<p>Answers directly, preserves causal detail across audiences and defends limits, alternatives and a specific verification plan.</p>

**Still needs evidence**

<p>Fluent narration or invented metrics without a trace, relevant artifact or honest evidence plan do not support the technical claim.</p>
